subject: Split-horizon AZ flap causing tail-latency & request failures
messages:
From: Alex Harper <alex@silverstream.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: ops-contact@silverstream.ai
Date: 2027-06-05T08:12:00-04:00
Subject: Intermittent timeouts + huge p99 latency in us-east-2

Jonas,

We started seeing a spike in 5xxs and p99 latency at ~07:50 ET for several of our realtime endpoints. Error rate went from ~0.2% to ~4% and traces show long tail latencies (15s+) from requests that route to your us-east-2 AZ. Customers are experiencing partial failures and we have a support page that is filling up with reports.

We are already diverting some traffic client-side but that's not ideal. Can Redwood temporarily steer traffic away from us-east-2 while you investigate? We need something that avoids client-side patching.

Alex
Sr. Platform Engineer
SilverStream Analytics

Immediate asks:

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: ava_chen@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-05T08:47:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent timeouts + huge p99 latency in us-east-2

On 2027-06-05 08:25, jonas_weber@redwood.ai wrote:
> Team — Alex reported an urgent customer impact (SilverStream). Summary: elevated 5xxs and p99 tail latency concentrated on us-east-2.

We're looking. Quick status: we attempted to create a per-account geo-split rule (SSD-9876) and seed diversion to us-east-1, but routing mesh shows inconsistent route advertisements across AZs — some requests still see us-east-2 endpoints.

Initial hypothesis: a split-horizon condition where the control plane update propagated to some edge clusters but stale route caches in a subset of the ingress pods are causing transient flaps between AZ endpoints. This results in replays/hard timeouts when sessions hit a node with a warmed KV cache pointing to an unhealthy AZ.

What we did:
- Triggered a targeted cache invalidation for the impacted prefix in us-east-2 (log: route-diff.log attached).
- Deployed a conservative 60/40 geo-split (East1/East2) for SSD-9876 to reduce blast radius.
- Opened a packet capture on a sample path (silverstream-pcap-snippet.txt attached).

Observed: p99 dropped from 15s to ~3.5s for ~55% of requests; however ~45% still show >10s depending on ingress pod. We need a coordinated drain of the stale routing table on affected nodes.

Next steps (need approvals):
1) Run a rolling drain for ingress pods in the affected AZ (will cause short conn churn) — estimated 12m per node; parallelism limited to 2 nodes at once.
2) If drain doesn't stabilize in 20m, escalate to full AZ evacuation for SSD-9876 (route all their traffic to us-east-1).

Requesting Marcus/Ava sign-off on the node-drain plan. I pushed a short dashboard screenshot to the incident channel (grafana-az-flap-spike.png).

Marissa Cole
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: route-diff.log, silverstream-pcap-snippet.txt, grafana-az-flap-spike.png
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Thanks Marissa — proceed with the rolling drain on ingress nodes in us-east-2. Keep parallelism at 2 nodes and track success metrics per drain. Escalate to AZ evacuation only if the drain fails to reduce p99 below 2s within 20m.

Also: brief COMM note for customer-facing team: "We're seeing routing table inconsistencies in us-east-2 that are causing increased tail latency for a subset of requests. We're actively draining impacted nodes and diverting traffic; we'll provide an update in 30 minutes." Vanessa, please send.

I'll join the bridge in 10.

Marcus Lin
VP, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-05T09:28:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent timeouts + huge p99 latency in us-east-2

Alex — quick update from our side: we are running a rolling drain of affected ingress pods in us-east-2 now and have applied a conservative geo-split to move the majority of your traffic to us-east-1. You should see reduced failures within the next 10–15 minutes.

If you can avoid any client-side recirculation for another 30m that will help stabilization. We're also preparing a temporary rate-limit knob you can toggle if you see any retry storms.

We're treating this as P1 and will follow up with a full postmortem and corrective actions (route cache reconciliation + improved control-plane anti-flap).

— Jonas

Attachments: none
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Date: 2027-06-05T14:03:00-04:00
Subject: Post-mitigation update: stabilization confirmed, next steps

Status update — as of 14:00 ET the drains completed on the targeted ingress nodes and the per-account geo-split has been removed; all SSD-9876 traffic now routes primarily to us-east-1.

Impact: error rate returned to baseline (~0.25%) and p99 is ~1.8s for the customer. We archived the pcap and logs to the incident bundle.

Action items for follow-up:
- Engineering: implement control-plane anti-flap debounce (owner: infra-core).
- SRE: add a route-cache invalidation API so we can avoid node drains in the future (owner: platform-tools).
- CS/AM: coordinate a customer goodwill ask (credits + 1:1 postmortem) — Jonas to own.
- Exec: recommend a temporary account credit for SilverStream to preserve relationship (Marcus to approve).

I'll prepare a detailed postmortem draft and send tomorrow.

Marissa Cole
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
